summary.oneLiner: Usha Martin Limited is a globally recognised manufacturer of high-quality steel wires, wire ropes, strands and LRPC, supplying application-specific solutions to oil and gas, mining, elevator, infrastructure, heavy engineering, shipping and logistics customers across six continents.
summary.business: Usha Martin manufactures wire ropes, steel wire, strands including locked coil, LRPC strand and conveyor cord, and sells standard as well as customised, application-specific solutions that meet global standards and certifications. currentContext.strengths: World-class manufacturing facilities delivering a wide range of standard and customised solutions that meet global standards and certifications|Broad product range across wire ropes, wire, strands, LRPC and conveyor cord, with a focus on customised, application-specific products|Global manufacturing and distribution network — production in India, the UK, the UAE and Thailand, plus warehousing/distribution and sales subsidiaries across Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and the Americas, with operational presence across six continents|Ability to shift production progressively to India for cost efficiency and local capabilities while retaining the international network for distribution and customer engagement|Digitalisation backbone — rollout of SAP Rise S/4HANA and customer relationship management systems improving process control, efficiency and customer engagement, with internal controls embedded in SAP S/4HANA|Standalone operations became debt-free as at 31st March 2026 following repayment of outstanding borrowings|Strengthening portfolio of customised and value-added products with greater emphasis on higher-margin segments with lower competitive intensity|Stable industrial relations supported by long-term wage agreements with recognised unions, and in-house skill building through the Usha Martin Learning Academy at Ranchi
currentContext.strategies: Compete in segments where performance, reliability and technical capability decide who wins — applications such as elevators, cranes, mines, ports and offshore installations where customers qualify suppliers rigorously and reward consistent quality, deep application knowledge and dependable service|Enrich the mix towards wire ropes and, within wire ropes, towards value-added products, and towards international markets — the shift that management identifies as a principal driver of the improvement in margins and returns|'One Usha Martin' — operate as a single company so every customer gets the Group's best engineering, most competitive manufacturing and deepest market knowledge, instead of each country business serving only its own market|Build a common operating foundation: common technology systems giving one view of customers, orders, inventory and performance; shared services for accounting, sales coordination and administrative support; centrally coordinated procurement and logistics; and KPIs across all entities aligned to Group-wide goals|Share market credentials globally — sales teams working from common playbooks, field-performance data and customer references, so a rope proven in one market becomes a credential in every market|Deploy the stronger (net cash) balance sheet judiciously into capacity, technology, product development and market expansion only where there is a clear customer opportunity, a sustainable competitive advantage and attractive long-term returns — and hold back where those conditions are not met|Improve execution pace so that capability becomes approvals, approvals become orders and orders become repeat business, thereby lifting utilisation of recently commissioned capacity and broadening its customer base|Release working capital through better forecasting, planning and collection discipline|Grow carefully chosen adjacencies next to the core: value-added automotive, transmission-line and rockfall-protection wires; plasticated LRPC strand for demanding bridge and stay-cable projects; and OceanFibre synthetic slings complementing steel wire ropes in offshore and marine applications|Optimise the manufacturing network by gradually increasing production in India for cost efficiency and local capabilities, while the international network supports distribution and customer engagement|Digitalise operations — SAP S/4HANA implemented across key global units (Singapore, Australia, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, US and UK) as an integrated, centralised digital backbone, with Salesforce CRM fully integrated into the SAP landscape|Stay focused on productivity, cost efficiency, working capital management and return on capital|The Company's declared dividend for FY 2025-26 is a final dividend of Rs. 3.75 per equity share of Re. 1 each, recommended by the Board and placed before shareholders for declaration as an ordinary resolution at the Fortieth Annual General Meeting. Remuneration of Directors, Senior Management Personnel and other employees is governed by a Board-approved Nomination & Remuneration Policy, and a Board-approved policy for identifying Material Subsidiaries is in place under Regulation 16(1)(c) of the SEBI Listing Regulations. No further reinvestment, buyback or leverage philosophy is set out in the routed governance sections.|Climate mitigation approach: reduce the carbon intensity of steel wire and rope making processes as part of a long-term strategy, shift toward cleaner energy alternatives, scale renewable energy capacity to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, and optimise production processes to minimise emissions associated with raw material consumption, with progress tracked and reported annually|External assurance on sustainability reporting: SGS India Private Limited provides Reasonable Assurance on BRSR core indicators and Limited Assurance on other indicators|CSR: although the Company is not statutorily required to incur CSR spending due to the absence of net profits under Section 198 over the last three financial years, it voluntarily carries out CSR activities through its CSR arm, the Usha Martin Foundation|Grievance redressal architecture across stakeholder groups — a community grievance email routed through the Usha Martin Foundation, an investor/shareholder redressal mechanism with a designated official, union interaction plus a monthly Shop Council for shop-floor worker grievances, whistle-blower reporting to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee, an Internal Committee for sexual harassment, a Customer Complaint Management System, and a channel for value chain partners|Sustainable procurement policy and supplier code of conduct extended to value chain partners|Human capital: building a future-ready workforce through the Usha Martin Learning Academy at Ranchi, a newly introduced Learning Management System, on-the-job and classroom training, town halls and feedback mechanisms, with a continuing stated focus on improving diversity and on a work environment supporting career growth and work-life balance
currentContext.expansion: Usha Martin is expanding capacity at its Ranchi facility with a focus on value-added products, positioning it to serve demand for crane and elevator ropes from Indian construction and urban infrastructure, conductor wires and LRPC strands from power transmission and bridge projects, and offshore, oil and gas, mining and crane ropes internationally. Alongside the Ranchi expansion the Company is integrating its global operations, streamlining processes and strengthening its supply chain, and has globally streamlined operations while gradually shifting more production to India to take advantage of cost efficiency and local capabilities, with the international network continuing to support distribution and customer engagement. Management notes that the Company has invested over recent years in additional capacity, technical capabilities and new products; these investments are progressing well but some are taking longer than anticipated to scale into meaningful commercial business because approval and product-development cycles in the industry are long, particularly in specialised applications, so the stated focus is to speed up the conversion of capability into approvals, approvals into orders and orders into repeat business, which will lift the utilisation of recently commissioned capacity and broaden the customer base it serves. The move from net debt to net cash is described as giving the Company flexibility to invest in capacity, technology, product development and market expansion while remaining prudent, with ongoing investments funded by strong cash flows and internal resources. Separately, the Company invested in digitalisation and technology, including the rollout of SAP Rise S/4HANA and customer relationship management systems, which improved process control, efficiency and customer engagement. No project-wise capex amounts, commissioning dates or installed-capacity figures are disclosed in the routed sections.
currentContext.mdna: Infrastructure-led growth in India — Government initiatives such as Viksit Bharat@2047, Bharatmala, Sagarmala, Smart Cities Mission and urban housing programmes are expected to drive sustained wire rope demand across construction, ports, mining and transportation|Urbanisation, particularly in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, plus housing, metro rail, high speed rail and airport projects, supporting the construction and elevator rope segments|Mining activity gaining momentum on policy support and higher domestic production, lifting demand for specialised mining solutions|Growth in oil and gas and maritime development (Sagarmala, Maritime India Vision) contributing to offshore, port and logistics demand|Offshore wind generating new demand for ropes in installation, lifting and mooring; offshore oil and gas remaining active as countries invest in energy security|Every rope is a consumable replaced on a safety-mandated cycle, so each installation won becomes recurring demand|Expansion of the domestic steel sector, supported by capacity additions and ongoing investments, further strengthening demand for wire rope products|International markets, particularly Europe and the United States, expected to provide further growth opportunities|Value-added and specialised products — synthetic slings, coated wires and application-specific solutions — expanding addressable markets and supporting margin improvement|Digitalisation, automation and analytics improving operational efficiency, cost optimisation and decision-making|Global supply chain realignment positioning India as a competitive manufacturing hub, an opportunity to strengthen exports|Cost control, supply chain efficiency and timely execution expected to support further improvement in performance|Headwinds flagged: geopolitical conflict in West Asia and disruption of routes such as the Strait of Hormuz; trade and tariff measures; price competition from low-cost East Asian manufacturers; and rising environmental and safety compliance costs|India GDP projected to grow by around 6.6% in FY 2026-27; global growth expected to moderate to around 3.1% in 2026-27

risks.note: Ongoing global conflicts, particularly in West Asia, and disruptions in key trade routes such as the Strait of Hormuz may impact supply chains, logistics costs and availability of raw materials for a business that runs long global supply chains.

Changes in global trade policies, including tariff measures and protectionist trends, may affect export competitiveness and market access in key geographies — material given the scale of the Company's international business.
Competition from low-cost manufacturers, especially from East Asian countries, continues to exert pressure on pricing and margins in certain product segments.
Increasing environmental and safety regulations across the markets served may lead to higher compliance costs and operational complexities.

risks.risk: Climate stewardship and energy transition (BRSR material issue, negative financial implication)
risks.note: Steel wire and rope production is inherently energy intensive. Limited green energy availability and high adoption costs may hinder decarbonisation, straining operational efficiency, escalating production expenses and delaying sustainability goals; tightening environmental regulation, evolving carbon pricing and the physical risk of extreme weather events affecting manufacturing continuity add further urgency.

Manufacturing processes generate air pollutants (PM, SOx, NOx). Non-compliance with permissible limits could trigger operational disruptions, regulatory penalties or licence revocations and damage reputation, while lagging global sustainability expectations may lead to financial losses and competitive disadvantage.
Exports contributed 35% of the entity's total turnover, so demand, tariff and currency conditions in overseas markets bear directly on the business.

Manufacturing of wire rope, wire and strands including locked coil accounted for 94.56% of the entity's turnover, leaving performance tied to one product family and its end-market cycles (wire rope alone 63.88%, wire and strands 17.13%, LRPC strand 13.55% of turnover).

one-line thesis: Usha Martin delivered record Q4 margins (21.6%) and turned net debt to net cash (INR 332 Cr) by shifting mix to high-value ropes and executing cost synergies, positioning the debt-free balance sheet to fund INR 300 Cr capex for 10-12% volume CAGR despite temporary Middle East headwinds.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 979 Cr (Q4, +9.3% YoY), INR 3,691 Cr (FY26, +6.2% YoY); EBITDA: INR 212 Cr (Q4, +52% YoY, 21.6% margin), INR 705 Cr (FY26, +18% YoY, 19.1% margin); PAT: INR 155 Cr (Q4), INR 491 Cr (FY26, up from INR 406 Cr); Order Book: Healthy visibility for H1 FY27 (unquantified), 85% replacement market; Net Debt: Net Cash INR 332 Cr (vs Net Debt INR 63 Cr in FY25) - One-offs: INR 19 Cr interest income from tax refund included in other income; Accounting Distortions: None noted, LRPC volume decline (-20.4%) artificially inflated mix-driven margins.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 10-12% volume CAGR expected for next 2-3 years; Margin: Minimum 20% operating margin benchmark (vs prior 18-19%); Order Inflow: Strong visibility for H1 FY27, especially in value-added segments; Capex/Commissioning: INR 300 Cr over next 2 years for elevator rope capacity (+6,000 tons), specialized wires, and plasticated LRPC expansion.
order book & pipeline: Management declined specific quantification but cited 'fairly healthy order book' for specialized projects and strong visibility for H1 FY27; 85% of business is replacement market providing stable baseline; Order inflow accelerating in oil & offshore, crane, and mining segments.
segment / subsidiary detail: Wire Ropes: Revenue +14.8% (Q4), +8% (FY26); Volume +5% (Q4, impacted by 900 ton Middle East loss); Realization >INR 300k/ton (first time); Wire: Revenue +31.2% (Q4), +24% (FY26); LRPC: Revenue -20.4% (Q4) due to strategic shift away from traditional 'black' LRPC to plasticated; International Revenue: 57% of total (up from 55%).
growth verticals / optionality: Plasticated LRPC: Approvals imminent (weeks), targeting scale-up from 2,500 tons to 4,000-6,000 tons annually; Synthetic Slings: Gaining traction with repeat orders; Parvatmala Project: Significant rope demand expected in 2-3 years as projects reach final stages; Thailand Plant: Modernization ongoing (18-month timeline) to produce specialized elevator/gondola cords; Market Share Expansion: Sub-5% in US and 10-12% in Europe offer runway for growth.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 Margin 21.6% driven by: 1) Product mix shift to high-value ropes (crane, mining, elevator); 2) 'One Usha Martin' savings (INR 65-70 Cr annualized: fixed employee costs -3%, admin -7%); 3) Full pass-through of input cost inflation (steel, gas); Cost Headwinds: LPG/Propane costs doubled (INR 60k to INR 120-130k/ton), impacting INR 2.5-3 Cr/month; Mitigation: 25% fuel switch to natural gas completed.
capex / expansion: INR 300 Cr planned over next 2 years; Allocation: 70-75% for wire rope capacity expansion (+6,000 tons, focused on elevator ropes); 25-30% for specialized wires and plasticated LRPC equipment/testing; Funding: Entirely through internal accruals (Net Cash position).
capital allocation: Priority 1: Organic capex (INR 300 Cr) for capacity expansion; Priority 2: Selective inorganic M&A in value-added/rigging to expand global footprint; Priority 3: Dividend payouts (attractive payout noted by analysts); Debt Strategy: Maintained net cash position, no leverage required for growth.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical: Middle East conflict causing project delays and supply chain disruption (900 ton volume impact in Q4); Input Costs: Volatility in steel rod and gas prices (though pass-through mechanism exists); Execution: Delays in customer approvals for plasticated LRPC could slow scale-up; Macro: Trade uncertainties/tariffs in US market.
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; Emphasized resilience of business model, successful navigation of geopolitical headwinds, and transition from deleveraging phase to growth phase; Focused on absolute EBITDA growth alongside margin expansion.
non-obvious takeaways: The 20% margin guidance is a structural step-up, not cyclical, driven by the permanent exit from low-margin steel business and the 'One Usha Martin' operating leverage; The company is effectively self-funding its entire growth capex while sitting on net cash, a rare profile in capital-intensive manufacturing; Middle East disruption is viewed as a temporary deferral with massive reconstruction upside once conflict resolves.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global energy security priorities driving offshore oil & wind capex; Need for high-spec ropes in deepwater projects | Usha Martin Ltd | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary via order book growth in oil/offshore segment; unique capability in large single-reel production (Oceanmax project) creates moat. |
| Middle East reconstruction post-conflict; Infrastructure rebuild requiring massive rope volumes | Usha Martin Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Only wire rope manufacturer in GCC region; well-positioned to capture reconstruction demand once geopolitical situation stabilizes. |
| Rising input costs (steel, gas) squeezing margins for competitors without pricing power | Unorganized Domestic Rope Manufacturers | loser | High | Usha's ability to fully pass through costs and shift mix to value-added products will likely steal share from smaller players unable to absorb inflation. |

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
